trace.final_message:
The new `hourglass/gaps.py` is written, tested and committed as `3572633`. The full suite passes (thirty-five tests, nine of them new) and the lint check is clean.

- **Main function:** `uncovered_labels(spans, opening)` returns one label per uncovered stretch, for example `gap 12:00-13:00 (60 min)`. Overlapping, touching and unsorted spans are handled by reusing `merge_spans`. If nobody works, the whole opening span comes back as one gap.
- **Exception:** a worked span that starts before opening or ends after closing raises the new `OutsideHoursError`. I made it a subclass of `ProjectError` in `hourglass/errors.py`, so existing handlers for that error will catch it. Its message is the offending span as text.
- **Helpers:** the module also has `check_inside`, `find_gaps` and `gap_label`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_gaps.py` covers a gap in the middle, full coverage, overlaps, no workers, gaps at both ends, touching spans, unsorted input, and both outside-hours cases.
- **Other edits:** I exported `uncovered_labels` and `OutsideHoursError` from `hourglass/__init__.py`. I also added a line to `docs/api.txt` and an entry under Unreleased in `CHANGES.txt`.

I followed the project conventions throughout: functions of eight lines or fewer, lines of sixty characters or fewer, reverse alphabetical imports, no trailing commas in multi-line calls, and variable names of four letters or more. I reviewed the staged diff before committing.

hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
